convoLines.text: "Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. I thought if you believed that, you'd trust me faster. I'm sorry. Or I'm supposed to be."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Sure. I'll be around."
«No entiendo nada. ¡Nada!»
«Eso mismo. Diste en el clavo.» — Grayson translates: "That's it. You hit the nail on the head." They nod back, a little quicker this time.
«No lo olvidaré.» — Grayson translates: "I won't forget it." A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Water?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Eres un sol, gracias de corazón.» — Grayson translates: "You're a sun, thanks from the heart." You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You lean in, catching the rise and fall of it. «¿Tú eres... el jefe?» — Grayson translates: "Are you... the boss?"
«¿Cuántos días llevamos aquí?» — Grayson translates: "How many days have we been here?"

Fernando tilts their head. "...What?" You try again, slower, redder. A long beat. Then the smallest smile. "Eso mismo. Diste en el clavo," they say — perfectly. "You meant." They knew all along; they just wanted to watch you work for it.
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
Groups make noise. Noise gets you noticed. I work better quiet.
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Grayson shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I like people fine. In doses. Small doses. With exits."
"I'll show up when it matters. The rest of the time, I'm elsewhere. That's the deal."
"Still on wanting to be left alone."
"Alone's how I stay alive. Don't take it personal."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"No, really — it's handled. Thanks for asking, though."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.

«Sí, sí, exacto.» — Grayson translates: "Yes, yes, exactly." They nod back, slowly. "You good?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Eres buena persona.» — Grayson translates: "You're a good person." They smile back, slower this time, like it just landed.
«Gracias. De verdad, gracias.» — Grayson translates: "Thanks. Truly, thanks." You press a hand to your own chest, then point at them. Together — they get it.
You hold still and let the sounds settle. «¿Dónde se duerme aquí?» — Grayson translates: "Where does one sleep here?"
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.

"Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
"You're kind. Don't let this place change that."
"I dreamed Atlas was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"I keep turning over the last thing Atlas said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."

"Sleep's gone strange. I rinse the cup twice at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. David Pawlowski is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ David is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer.
d41: 🕯️ David Pawlowski is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What David kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "David's gone." Atlas looks at you for a long moment. "You're not David." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Cameron blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Fire in Rain (Level 1). Split wood — the inside is dry even when the outside is soaked. Feather sticks catch fast.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Draw Fire (Level 1). In the wilds, beside your people, you make yourself the problem. Shout, wave, bleed loudly — the beast's eye stays on you and off them. Monsters focus you instead of your allies.

d41: 📖 LEARNED: Rally (Level 1). In the wilds, when the fight is lost and running would be sane, you look at the people standing with you and you do not run. Once per fight, when the trajectory turns hopeless and an ally stands beside you, you hold the line instead of fleeing. Not volume — a promise kep
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: David Pawlowski, 41 days. The mantle passes to Cameron Santiago.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Cameron Santiago, 45 — a Firefighter. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Berserker Rage.
d41: The village's quarrel was with David — and David is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Atlas, Grayson, Fernando and 3 more speak for Cameron — "David trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Cameron before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
